text:
maya: hey team 👋 first-day kubectl weirdness. I ran `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` and `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-onboard` but `kubectl get pods -n maya-dev` returns Forbidden. `kubectl config get-contexts` shows two contexts (one arn style, one named `dev-team`). Not sure which to use.

sam: welcome! if you see an arn-style context that comes from the EKS helper. Can you paste the `users:` exec block from `kubectl config view --raw`? should show `aws eks get-token` and the AWS_PROFILE.

maya: paste: `users:
- name: arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev
  user:
    exec:
      apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1
      command: aws
      args:
      - eks
      - get-token
      - --cluster-name
      - redwood-dev
      - --region
      - us-west-2
      - --profile
      - redwood-onboard
      env:
      - name: AWS_PROFILE
        value: redwood-onboard`

diana: that looks normal. Forbidden means RBAC: your SSO principal isn't bound to a RoleBinding in `maya-dev`. New hires usually get a namespace-scoped binding called `onboard-edit`. File the Kubernetes access form (choose Kubernetes namespace access, namespace=maya-dev, role=onboard-edit).

maya: where do I file it? I can't find the link in the handbook.

sam: https://redwood.example.com/access -> select "Kubernetes namespace access". If you want a faster workaround you can request a temporary ServiceAccount kubeconfig in the form notes and ping infra oncall.

maya: ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n maya-dev` -> no. filed the form and pinged infra oncall.

infra-bot: access request created by maya at 2034567012 — id K-55900. Assigned to infra oncall. ETA ~1h.

infra-oncall: got it, thanks @maya. quick note: after infra creates the RoleBinding, you MUST re-run `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` so your SSO session picks up the role mapping. Then `aws eks get-token --cluster-name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-onboard` should return a token with the new permissions.

maya: infra approved, re-ran `aws sso login` and `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n maya-dev` -> yes! `kubectl get pods -n maya-dev` works now. thank you.

diana: one extra tip for folks merging kubeconfigs from other employers: use a separate file for redwood and merge intentionally. e.g. `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood:~/.kube/config` then `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` to make a clean merge. if you just want to avoid the old contexts, `kubectl config delete-context <old>` or `kubectl config rename-context <old> <old-backup>`.

sam: and tiny dotfiles helper I drop in my shell: `kuse(){ kubectl config use-context "$(kubectl config get-contexts -o name | grep -i "$1" | head -n1)"; }` so `kuse redwood` will pick the first matching context name.

maya: bookmarking both suggestions. also FYI the SA kubeconfig flow infra offered is temporary (4h) and namespace-scoped — good to know if you need fast iteration before RBAC is set.

diana: welcome aboard again! ping #dev-ex if you want a quick walkthrough for port-forwarding and sane kubeconfig cleanup. :party_parrot:
